contentBody: **After you pick one idea, what should a refine step make clear?**
option.1: Payments, ratings, and a map so the idea looks already complete
option.2: The user, the problem, the first version, and what to leave out
option.3: Invented survey percentages so the idea sounds already proven
option.4: A request that the model praise the idea and hide any remaining risk
answerExplanation: Refine narrows one winner. Naming what the first version must not do stops a feature pile. Invented numbers and praise are not a refine.

contentBody: **Which target user is specific enough to stress-test?**
option.1: Anyone in the country who owns a mobile phone
option.2: Students in general, in any city, at any hour
option.3: One kind of person, in a real place, at the moment of pain
option.4: People who will appear only after a huge advertising campaign
answerExplanation: “Everyone” and “students” are too wide. A stress-test needs a person you could actually meet, plus when the pain happens.

contentBody: **Why should you reject a value line packed with words such as ecosystem and revolutionary?**
option.1: Those words are required on every professional landing page
option.2: Models refuse to generate any sentence that omits those words
option.3: A classmate can always repeat a jargon line after hearing it once
option.4: They hide the user, the job, and the pain the offer should name
answerExplanation: Jargon is not a value proposition. If a classmate cannot repeat the line, it is still too vague or too decorated.
